term: present ought-implies-can and same-action duty retention
definition: PresentOIC requires each action owed after the loss to be practically possible at that date. InitialDuty and PresentDuty fix the SAME originalReturn at before and after. Retention is its before-to-after implication. PresentInability denies that SAME after action ability. FutureOIC instead asks for some strictly later practical ability for each action owed after. futureRepair requires a separate duty-to-ideal interpretation and ideal/future overlap; these are explicit assumptions, not independently vindicated moral facts. LocalOIC is the weaker sibling restricted to originalReturn only: PresentDuty s → s.able after originalReturn. It does not imply compensation or debt-repayment OIC, even with a nonvacuous original-return duty. Universal PresentOIC strictly strengthens LocalOIC.
note: No cancellation, compensation, culpability-to-duty or descriptive-to-normative bridge is built in. These policies are conditional inputs; their applicability and truth remain open.
